post.summary: Fetch a registered agent's card, verify it against the operator's out-of-band root, and report the fingerprint. Approves nothing and writes nothing

200.description: OK (the derived trust state and the fingerprint a human is being asked to approve; a card that could not be authenticated is still a 200 — the reason is in `failure` and the state is `error`)

post.summary: Lock a registered agent to the card fingerprint the operator has SEEN. The card is re-fetched and re-verified, and an approval naming any other fingerprint is refused

200.description: OK (the registration's state AFTER the approval, read off the live registry)

A2aTrustView.description:
THE TRUST VIEW of one registered agent — what both verbs answer with.

The sibling of the tool-serving plane's trust view and shaped like it on purpose: an
operator console rendering both planes should be rendering one component. It is NOT the same
type, because the two planes' capability vocabularies differ (a `tools:` entry has an approved
digest per tool; an `agents:` entry has a skill set on a card) and merging them would mean one
of the planes filling in fields that mean nothing to it.

changed.description: Approved, but offered at a DIFFERENT digest. THIS IS THE RUG-PULL ROW.

failure.description: Why the contact failed, when it did.

fingerprint.description:
THE CANONICAL CARD FINGERPRINT AN OPERATOR IS BEING ASKED TO APPROVE. Surfaced explicitly
rather than left for a caller to dig out, because this is the one string that goes in front
of the human and `approve` refuses anything else.

observed_skills.description: How many skills the observation carried.

pin_changed.description:
The presented identity is not the locked one. Its own axis: adopting a new identity is a
different act from adopting new content.

pin_mechanism.description:
The operator's word for the authenticity root, as the OBSERVED pin names it. Never
interpreted by the machine.

state.description:
`pending`, `approved`, `quarantined`, `suspended` or `error`. DERIVED on every read from the
standing approval and the sighting, so there is no stored state to go stale.

ApproveReq.description:
The `approve` request body. ONE required field, and it is required because it is the operator's
evidence that they looked.

fingerprint.description: The canonical card fingerprint EXACTLY as `connect` reported it.

label: A2A
caller_credential_refusal: `upstream_credentials: passthrough` is refused on the `agents:` plane. busbar delegates AS ITSELF: the caller's key authenticated them to busbar and means nothing to a third-party agent, so forwarding it would hand that agent a working busbar credential belonging to someone else. Use `own` with an `upstream_credential:` handle.
